ca630e5412bbe3.s: The World Health Organization, established in 1948, is headquartered in:
ca630e5412bbe3.x: The WHO, established in 1948 and led by Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, is headquartered in Geneva.

ca55a1a446de7b.s: The Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement (CCRA), whose Development Board India chairs for 2026–28, deals with:
o: Reduction of tariffs on IT products
Mutual recognition of IT security certificates
ca55a1a446de7b.x: The CCRA concerns mutual recognition of IT security certificates; India chairs its Development Board for 2026–28.

cafdcbf2e0381a.s: Under the India–New Zealand FTA, India will remove or reduce tariffs on about what share of imports from New Zealand?
cafdcbf2e0381a.x: India will remove or reduce tariffs on about 95% of imports from New Zealand, while New Zealand eliminates tariffs on 100% of goods from India.

cad99a20bcf069.s: What is the capital of Trinidad and Tobago, visited by S. Jaishankar?
cad99a20bcf069.x: The capital of Trinidad and Tobago is Port of Spain, not San Fernando.

ca3b8086f2409d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Turkey's proposed social media curbs?
o: The Bill restricts social media for children below 15
The capital of Turkey is Istanbul
Platforms such as YouTube and TikTok must verify age
The Bill provides for parental controls
ca3b8086f2409d.x: The capital of Turkey is Ankara, not Istanbul; the Bill restricts social media for children below 15.

ca42dfd23f9a5e.s: What is India's status with regard to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)?
o: India signed it but has not ratified it
India is not a signatory and calls it discriminatory
India joined it at its indefinite extension in 1995
ca42dfd23f9a5e.x: India is not a signatory to the NPT and considers the treaty discriminatory.

ca31dde1721be9.s: The India–EU Trade and Technology Council, under which the EV Battery Recycling initiative runs, was launched in:
ca31dde1721be9.x: The India–EU TTC was launched in 2022; the €15.2 million battery recycling initiative operates under it.

caab477801c1b2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the World Bank's Water Forward programme?
o: It seeks water security for 1 billion people by 2030
It is delivered through country-led Water Compacts
The World Bank Group alone is to reach 600 million of the 1 billion
It was launched by WBG President Ajay Banga
caab477801c1b2.x: The World Bank Group is to reach 400 million people and partners 600 million; the other statements are correct.

ca0279d0be07ec.s: Under the India–EU FTA, the EU offered commitments in how many services subsectors?
ca0279d0be07ec.x: The EU offered commitments in 144 services subsectors and India in 102.

caca45064c1f63.s: After legal scrubbing, the India–EU FTA must be ratified by the European Parliament and how many EU member states?
caca45064c1f63.x: Ratification is by the 27 EU member states and the European Parliament.

ca9c01e6ba5552.s: Which of the following was NOT excluded by India from its commitments under the India–Oman CEPA?
o: Gold and silver bullion and jewellery
ca9c01e6ba5552.x: India's exclusions include dairy, tea, bullion and jewellery, footwear and sports goods; petroleum and crude are not excluded.

caa74a72972878.s: In which category was India re-elected to the IMO Council for 2026–27, with 154 of 169 votes?
caa74a72972878.x: India was re-elected to the IMO Council in Category B with the highest votes, 154 of 169.

ca1762aa0c7e3c.s: The High-level Political Forum run by the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) deals with:
ca1762aa0c7e3c.x: ECOSOC runs the High-level Political Forum on the Sustainable Development Goals, not on international trade.

ca91ccb682f432.s: The Maritime Labour Convention 2006, the 'Seafarers' Bill of Rights', was adopted at the International Labour Conference in:
ca91ccb682f432.x: The MLC 2006 was adopted on 23 February 2006 at the International Labour Conference in Geneva, not London.

caaac6e1ab1117.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Eurozone and Bulgaria?
o: The Eurozone had 20 members before Bulgaria joined
Bulgaria is scheduled to join the Eurozone in 2027
Bulgaria replaced the lev with the euro
Bulgaria became the 21st EU country to adopt the euro
caaac6e1ab1117.x: Bulgaria joined the Eurozone in 2026, not 2027, becoming the 21st member after the earlier 20.

ca93e6aeae6976.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–Euratom Agreement?
o: It covers peaceful, civilian nuclear cooperation
Euratom was set up in 1957 by the Treaty of Rome
ca93e6aeae6976.x: India–Euratom cooperation is civilian only; Euratom is headquartered in Brussels, not Geneva.

cafb20465ac924.s: Which European countries were reluctant to recognise Palestine because of their Holocaust legacy?
cafb20465ac924.x: Germany and Austria were reluctant because of their Holocaust legacy; Spain, Ireland and Norway recognised Palestine.

ca4f32ab02f4f0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rubella and Nepal?
o: Nepal was first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to adopt a laboratory algorithm for rubella surveillance
The MMR vaccine requires three doses
Rubella is also called German measles
WHO declared Nepal free of rubella as a public health problem in August 2025
ca4f32ab02f4f0.x: The MMR vaccine has two doses, not three; the other statements are correct.

cafda7b30fe9a8.s: The India–ILO MoU, rooted in India's 2023 G20 presidency, concerns the development of the:
cafda7b30fe9a8.x: India and the ILO agreed to develop the International Reference Classification of Occupations (IRCO), following the G20's 2023 endorsement of skills-based migration pathways.

cae0f5bf1eed2a.s: The US H-1B visa is an example of which type of migration seen since the 1990s?
cae0f5bf1eed2a.x: Skilled migration has existed since the 1990s, the US H-1B being an example; GCC countries host mainly temporary labour migrants.

ca146fd4600a5e.s: The PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana targets how many formal jobs in two years?
ca146fd4600a5e.x: The Yojana targets 35 million formal jobs in two years.

ca1bd69b71de54.s: The Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act was enacted in:
ca1bd69b71de54.x: The CLND Act is of 2010; the Atomic Energy Act is of 1962.

ca191f4b62338f.s: Under the 2015 India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, how many people from Indian enclaves in Bangladesh migrated to India?
ca191f4b62338f.x: 922 people from Indian enclaves in Bangladesh migrated to India; 14,854 residents became new Indian citizens.

ca985198ac6eea.s: Which country hosted the Oslo Accords in 1993?
ca985198ac6eea.x: Norway hosted the Oslo Accords in 1993; it is also among the European states that recognised Palestine.

new.s: OPEC, which the UAE is leaving from 1 May 2026, is headquartered in:
new.x: OPEC, founded in 1960, is headquartered in Vienna, Austria, not Riyadh or Abu Dhabi.

new.s: In which month did the USA withdraw from the WHO?
new.x: The USA left the WHO in January 2026; Argentina left in March 2026.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of OPEC before the UAE's exit?
new.x: OPEC's 12 members included Gabon, Congo and Equatorial Guinea; Oman was not a member.

new.s: Withdrawal from the WHO after one year's notice, as by Argentina, follows which convention?
o: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, 1969
new.x: Withdrawal with one year's notice follows the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969).

new.s: OPEC+, made up of 12 OPEC and 10 non-OPEC countries, accounts for about what share of global crude?
new.x: OPEC+ (12 + 10 countries) together produces about 59% of global crude.

new.s: Talks on the India–New Zealand FTA, among India's fastest, were concluded in:
new.x: Talks began in March 2025 and concluded in December 2025; the FTA was signed on 27 April 2026.

new.s: Under a Free Trade Agreement, Rules of Origin are used to prevent:
new.x: Rules of Origin prevent trade deflection under an FTA.

new.s: India chaired the Kimberley Process earlier in:
new.x: India's 2026 chairship of the Kimberley Process is its third, after 2008 and 2019.

new.s: How many participants does the Kimberley Process have?
new.x: The Kimberley Process has 60 participants, with the EU counted as one (59 + EU).

new.s: India's election as Chair of the Common Criteria Development Board (2026–28) was announced at the CCRA meeting in:
new.x: India was elected CCDB Chair for April 2026–April 2028, announced at the CCRA meeting in Tokyo (14–16 April 2026).

new.s: The International Solar Alliance, which Romania joined as a full member in March 2026, is headquartered in:
new.x: The ISA, launched in 2015 by India and France at COP21, is headquartered in Gurugram.

new.s: When Romania signed the ISA Framework Agreement in December 2023, it became the ISA's:
new.x: Romania signed in December 2023 as the 118th member and ratified the Framework Agreement in March 2026.

new.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched in 2015 at:
new.x: The ISA was launched in 2015 by India and France at COP21 in Paris.

new.s: Chile became the first country in the Americas to eliminate leprosy, and the second in the world after:
new.x: Chile is first in the Americas and second globally after Jordan to eliminate leprosy as a public health problem.

new.s: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) is headquartered in:
new.x: PAHO is headquartered in Washington, D.C.

new.s: UNMISS, renewed by the UN Security Council to 30 April 2027, is the UN mission in:
new.x: UNMISS is the UN Mission in South Sudan, renewed for one year to 30 April 2027 with a reduced troop ceiling.

new.s: Which of the following UN peacekeeping missions is INCORRECTLY matched with its location?
new.x: UNIFIL is in Lebanon and runs a final mandate to 31 December 2026; UNMISS is the mission in South Sudan.

new.s: India's nomination for the UNESCO World Heritage 2025–26 cycle is:
new.x: India nominated the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath near Varanasi for the 2025–26 cycle.

new.s: The 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in July 2026, the first in Korea, is to be held at:
new.x: The 48th World Heritage Committee is at Busan, South Korea (July 2026), the first such session in Korea.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty:
1. It was opened for signature in 1968.
2. It came into force in 1975.
3. It was extended indefinitely in 1995.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NPT opened for signature in 1968, came into force in 1970 (not 1975) and was extended indefinitely in 1995.

new.s: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), headquartered in Vienna, is headed by Director General:
new.x: The IAEA (est. 1957, HQ Vienna) is headed by Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi.

new.s: Under the NPT, nuclear-weapon states are those that tested a nuclear device before:
new.x: Nuclear-weapon states are those that tested before 1 January 1967: the US, Russia, the UK, France and China.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Council of Europe?
o: It is an EU body with 27 members
new.x: The Council of Europe (1949, Strasbourg, 46 members) is not an EU body; the EU has 27 members and is based in Brussels.

new.s: The ENMOD Convention bans:
new.x: The ENMOD Convention bans hostile environmental modification techniques.

new.s: The term 'ecocide' was coined in 1970 by biologist:
new.x: Arthur W. Galston coined 'ecocide' in 1970 in the context of the Vietnam War and Agent Orange.

new.s: The 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14) in March 2026 was held at:
new.x: MC14 was held at Yaoundé, Cameroon, on 26–29 March 2026.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO's MC14:
1. It ended without agreement on WTO reform.
2. It renewed the e-commerce customs duty moratorium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: MC14 ended without agreement on its main issues, and the e-commerce moratorium was not renewed and lapsed.

new.s: Under WTO rules, public stockholding for food security falls under the criteria of the:
new.x: Public stockholding for food security falls in the Green Box criteria; trade-distorting price support is Amber.

new.s: The Amber Box de minimis limit for developing countries is:
new.x: The Amber Box de minimis is 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Dunkel Draft (20 December 1991) was the Uruguay Round Draft Final Act, not a Doha Round text.

new.s: How many members does the World Bank Group have?
new.x: The World Bank Group has 189 members; the World Bank was set up in 1944.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five arms of the World Bank Group?
new.x: The five arms are IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID; the AIIB is not part of the World Bank Group.

new.s: In its April 2026 World Economic Outlook, the IMF projected India's growth for FY27 at:
new.x: The April 2026 WEO projected India's growth at 6.5% for FY27 and cut global growth for 2026 to 3.1%.

new.s: Who is the President of the World Bank Group who launched 'Water Forward' in April 2026?
new.x: WBG President Ajay Banga launched Water Forward on 15 April 2026.

new.s: Who, as IMF Managing Director, urged completion of the 16th General Review of Quotas in April 2026?
new.x: IMF MD Kristalina Georgieva urged completion of the 16th General Review of Quotas at the 2026 Spring Meetings.

new.s: Which currency has the second-largest weight in the IMF's SDR basket?
new.x: The SDR weights are: US dollar 43.38%, euro 29.31%, renminbi 12.28%, yen 7.59%, pound 7.44%.

new.s: India's voting share in the IMF is about:
new.x: India's quota is about 2.75% (SDR 13,114.4 million) and its voting share about 2.63%; it is the 8th-largest quota holder.

new.s: The World Bank's USD 299.66 million Clean Air Management Program (March 2026) is for which state?
new.x: The UP Clean Air Management Program, signed on 16 March 2026, is part of the Indo-Gangetic Plains air quality programme.

new.s: India's first World Bank Step-Up Loan (April 2026) was approved for:
new.x: The USD 225 million Rajasthan Highway Modernisation Project is India's first Step-Up Loan.

new.s: The Borrowers' Platform launched at the IMF–World Bank Spring Meetings 2026 is NOT:
o: A forum to strengthen debt management
A coordination forum for debtor nations
new.x: The Borrowers' Platform is a coordination forum for debtor nations, not a debt restructuring mechanism.

new.s: Whose signature will appear on US currency notes from June 2026, the first time for a sitting President?
new.x: Donald Trump's signature will appear first on the $100 note in June 2026, marking the 250th Independence Day.

new.s: India supplied 1,000 MT of rice as aid to which country?
new.x: India sent 1,000 MT rice to Burkina Faso; Seychelles received 250 MT food grains.

new.s: The European Union is India's FTA partner number:
new.x: The EU is India's 22nd FTA partner; India has 15 FTAs covering 27 countries.

new.s: Under the India–EU FTA, what share of India's exports become duty-free at once?
new.x: 90.7% of India's exports become duty-free at once; 92.1% and 97% are the tariff lines liberalised by India and the EU.

new.s: Bulgaria and Romania became full members of the Schengen area from:
new.x: Bulgaria and Romania became full Schengen members from 1 January 2025.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the sectors India protected under the India–EU FTA?
new.x: India protected dairy, cereals, poultry and soymeal; textiles are among the labour-intensive gainers.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of India's trade agreements is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: CECPA is with Mauritius (2021); the UAE agreement is a CEPA (2022).

new.s: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), with which India restarted FTA talks in 2026, is headquartered in:
new.x: The GCC, established in 1981, is headquartered in Riyadh.

new.s: Under the India–Oman CEPA, the quota for Intra-Corporate Transferees rises from 20% to:
new.x: The Mode 4 quota for Intra-Corporate Transferees rises from 20% to 50%.

new.s: India's first trade agreement with an African nation was the 2021 CECPA with:
new.x: The India–Mauritius CECPA (2021) was India's first trade pact with an African nation.

new.s: India was elected unopposed to the UN Human Rights Council for 2026–28 for the:
new.x: India was elected for the 7th time, unopposed, for 1 January 2026 – 31 December 2028.

new.s: International IDEA, which India chairs from 1 January 2026, is headquartered in:
new.x: International IDEA (est. 1995) is headquartered in Stockholm.

new.s: India took over the BRICS presidency for 2026 from:
new.x: India holds the BRICS presidency from 1 January to 31 December 2026, taking over from Brazil.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the UN bodies in which India sits from 2026:
1. The UN Human Rights Council has 47 members and is based in Geneva.
2. ECOSOC has 54 members.
3. UNHRC members may serve any number of consecutive terms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: UNHRC has 47 members (Geneva) and ECOSOC 54; UNHRC members may serve at most two consecutive terms.

new.s: Which country is serving its first-ever term on the UN Security Council in 2026–27?
new.x: Latvia is the first-time member among the five elected for 2026–27.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT newly elected to the UN Security Council for 2026–27?
new.x: Pakistan is a continuing member elected in 2024; Bahrain, Colombia, DR Congo, Latvia and Liberia are new.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the G4?
new.x: The G4 are India, Germany, Japan and Brazil.

new.s: The Maritime Labour Convention 2006 is described as which pillar of international maritime law?
new.x: The MLC 2006 is called the 'fourth pillar' of international maritime law; it consolidated 60+ earlier ILO maritime conventions.

new.s: The US exit from UNESCO announced in January 2026 is its:
new.x: It is the US's third UNESCO exit, after 1984 and 2017.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about US withdrawals in January 2026:
1. A memorandum listed 66 bodies to quit, both UN and non-UN.
2. The US left the Paris Agreement for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The memorandum covered 66 bodies (35 non-UN + 31 UN); the US left the Paris Agreement a second time.

new.s: How many members does the World Health Organization have?
new.x: The WHO (est. 7 April 1948, HQ Geneva) has 194 members.

new.s: The USA is the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from which treaty?
new.x: The US is the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from the UNFCCC.

new.s: Under the Maastricht criteria for joining the Eurozone, government debt must be below what share of GDP?
new.x: Eurozone entry needs a deficit below 3% and debt below 60% of GDP, plus ERM II.

new.s: The UNESCO Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Alliance was launched in 2013 at:
new.x: The MIL Alliance was launched in 2013 at Abuja, Nigeria; it elected its first Global Board in January 2026.

new.s: In February 2026, the WHO validated Libya for eliminating which disease as a public health problem?
new.x: Libya eliminated trachoma, becoming the 28th country worldwide and 8th in the Eastern Mediterranean Region.

new.s: Which became the first EU country validated by the WHO for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis?
new.x: Denmark was validated on 27 February 2026, the first EU country.

new.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement is the second instrument adopted under which Article of the WHO Constitution?
new.x: It is the second instrument under Article 19, after the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the WHO Pandemic Agreement:
1. It was adopted by the World Health Assembly on 20 May 2025.
2. It is open for signature though the PABS annex is pending.
3. It enters into force after 60 ratifications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It was adopted on 20 May 2025 and needs 60 ratifications; it opens for signature only after the PABS annex is adopted.

new.s: MONUSCO, extended by the UN Security Council until 20 December 2026, is the UN mission in:
new.x: MONUSCO is in the DR Congo; the UNSC extended it unanimously in December 2025.

new.s: Which of the following UN peacekeeping missions is correctly matched?
new.x: UNIFIL is in Lebanon; MONUSCO is in DR Congo, MINURSO in Western Sahara and MINUSCA in the Central African Republic.

new.s: The IMF's World Economic Outlook Update of January 2026 projected India's growth for FY26 at:
new.x: The IMF raised India's FY26 projection to 7.3%; the World Bank's GEP put it at 7.2%.

new.s: The World Bank's Global Economic Prospects (January 2026) projected world growth for 2026 at:
new.x: The GEP projected world growth at 2.6% for 2026, down from 2.7% in 2025.

new.s: How many members does the IMF have?
new.x: The IMF has 191 members.

new.s: The IMF's 16th General Review of Quotas needs the consent of members holding what share of quotas?
new.x: It needs consent from members with 85% of quotas; by October 2025 only 72.78% had consented.

new.s: Which currency has the smallest weight in the IMF's SDR basket?
new.x: The pound has 7.44%, just below the yen at 7.59%; the dollar (43.38%) has the largest.

new.s: WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, who began a second four-year term in September 2025, is from:
new.x: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is from Nigeria; her second term began on 1 September 2025.

new.s: The 13th WTO Ministerial Conference (2024), which kept the e-commerce moratorium only until MC14, was held at:
new.x: MC13 was held at Abu Dhabi in 2024; it kept the moratorium (in place since 1998) until MC14 or 31 March 2026.

new.s: The Dunkel Draft, the basis of the WTO, was the Draft Final Act of which round?
new.x: The Dunkel Draft (20 December 1991), named after GATT DG Arthur Dunkel, was the Uruguay Round Draft Final Act.

new.s: Which WTO box covers minimally trade-distorting support with no limit?
new.x: The Green Box covers minimally distorting support with no limit, including public stockholding for food security.

new.s: The World Bank's USD 245 million READY-HP programme (February 2026) is for disaster recovery in:
new.x: READY-HP is Resilient Action for Development and Disaster Recovery Himachal Pradesh.

new.s: The UN World Food Programme, which signed a rice supply agreement with India, is headquartered in:
new.x: The WFP (est. 1961) is headquartered in Rome; its Executive Director is Cindy McCain.

new.s: The International Criminal Court, established in 2002, has its seat at:
new.x: The ICC, the first permanent international criminal court, sits at The Hague.

new.s: The International Criminal Court works on the principle of:
new.x: The ICC works on the principle of complementarity and tries war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide and aggression.

new.s: How many of the 193 UN members recognise Palestine?
new.x: 147 of 193 UN members recognise Palestine; the latest before September 2025 was Mexico (January 2025).

new.s: Which country recognised Palestine in January 2025, the latest before the September 2025 UNGA?
new.x: Mexico recognised Palestine in January 2025; Spain, Ireland and Norway had recognised earlier.

new.s: The Maratha Military Landscapes of India were inscribed in July 2025 at the World Heritage Committee session held in:
new.x: They were inscribed on 11 July 2025 at the 47th session in Paris, becoming India's 44th World Heritage property.

new.s: Which fort of the Maratha Military Landscapes of India is located in Tamil Nadu?
new.x: The serial nomination has 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu.

new.s: Which treaty governs the protection of cultural property in armed conflict?
new.x: The 1954 Hague Convention protects cultural property in armed conflict; Israel is a signatory.

new.s: Which Gaza site is described as the second-oldest mosque in Palestine?
new.x: The 7th-century Great Omari Mosque is the second-oldest mosque in Palestine.

new.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, needs how many countries for entry into force?
new.x: It needs 60 countries; the committee vote before adoption was 124 in favour, 0 against, 11 abstentions.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the WHO Pandemic Agreement:
1. It was adopted by the World Health Assembly on 20 May 2025.
2. It opened for signature on the day of its adoption.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It was adopted on 20 May 2025 but opens for signature only after the PABS Annex is adopted.

new.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025 caps nuclear liability at:
new.x: The SHANTI Act caps nuclear liability at 300 million SDRs (about ₹3,900 crore).

new.s: The India–US civil nuclear deal was signed in:
new.x: The India–US civil nuclear deal dates to 2008.

new.s: Who was the ILO Director-General who signed the IRCO MoU with India in Geneva?
new.x: The MoU was signed by Ambassador Arindam Bagchi and ILO DG Gilbert F. Houngbo.

new.s: The annual US H-1B quota, in place since 2004, is:
new.x: The H-1B quota is 85,000 a year, including 20,000 for US advanced degrees.

new.s: India's largest supplier of imported corn in 2024–25 was:
new.x: Myanmar supplied 0.53 mt and Ukraine 0.39 mt; the US only 1,100 tonnes.

new.s: Under the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement, how many Indian enclaves in Bangladesh were transferred to Bangladesh?
new.x: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh; 51 Bangladeshi enclaves merged into India.

new.s: The 51 Bangladeshi enclaves merged into India under the LBA 2015 were in:
new.x: The 51 Bangladeshi enclaves were in Cooch Behar, West Bengal.

new.s: UNIFIL, renewed 'for a final time' by UNSC Resolution 2790, is the UN Interim Force in:
new.x: UNIFIL is the UN Interim Force in Lebanon; Resolution 2790 was adopted on 28 August 2025.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about UNIFIL:
1. It was renewed by UNSC Resolution 2790 in August 2025.
2. Its mandate ended on 31 December 2025.
3. About 10,800 personnel are to withdraw within one year of its mandate end.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Its mandate ends on 31 December 2026, not 2025; withdrawal of about 10,800 personnel follows within one year.

new.s: The first WTO fisheries subsidies deal, banning subsidies to illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, was reached at MC12 in:
new.x: MC12 (2022) in Geneva produced the first fisheries subsidies deal.

new.s: The WTO e-commerce moratorium, which lapsed for the first time at MC14 in March 2026, had been in place since:
new.x: The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 30 March 2026 at MC14 (Yaoundé), the first time since 1998.

new.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies entered into force on 15 September 2025 after acceptance by how many members?
new.x: It entered into force after acceptances by two-thirds (111) of WTO members.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about WTO subsidy boxes?
o: Amber Box support is trade-distorting and capped
Blue Box support is exempt from reduction
The Amber de minimis for developing countries is 10%
Green Box support is capped at 5%
new.x: Green Box support is unlimited; the 5% de minimis applies to Amber Box support of developed countries.

new.s: The interim 'peace clause' agreed at Bali (2013) protects developing countries on:
new.x: The Bali peace clause shields developing countries breaching de minimis limits on public stockholding for food security.

new.s: Which country became the 191st member of the IMF on 21 October 2024?
new.x: Liechtenstein joined as the 191st member with a quota of SDR 100 million.

new.s: How many member countries does the IBRD have?
new.x: The IBRD has 189 members, while the IMF has 191.

new.s: In the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023, India ranked:
new.x: India ranked 38th of 139, up from 44th in 2018 and 54th in 2014.

new.s: Which lender approved a $788.8 million results-based loan in December 2024 for Amaravati capital Phase-I?
new.x: The ADB approved $788.8 million and the World Bank $800 million, together about $1.6 billion for Amaravati.

new.s: The World Bank loan for the Amaravati Integrated Urban Development Program is of:
new.x: The World Bank approved $800 million on 19 December 2024 (29 years incl. 6-year grace); $207 million was the first tranche.

new.s: Who is the Managing Director of the IMF?
new.x: Kristalina Georgieva is the IMF Managing Director.
